assertions.title: Agent card click opens detail panel
test_names: Step 1-3: Open agent panel and verify Info tab
logs tab exists and opens from agent detail panel
assertions.notes: agent-review-journey clicks ember agent button and asserts agent-detail-panel data-state=open. log-streaming.openEmberLogs() also verifies the panel opens via card click.

assertions.title: Panel header shows agent avatar, name, and status
test_names: Step 1-3: Open agent panel and verify Info tab
assertions.notes: Test verifies agent name in panel.locator('h2') ("ember"). Avatar element, status dot color, and sticky header scroll behavior are not asserted.

assertions.title: Five tabs render in order: Info, Logs, Git, Diff, Files
test_names: Step 1-3: Open agent panel and verify Info tab
Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
Step 7-8: Diff tab renders files, expand shows diff viewer
Step 9: Files tab renders file explorer
logs tab exists and opens from agent detail panel
assertions.notes: agent-review-journey covers Info/Git/Diff/Files via getByRole('tab', { name: ... }). log-streaming asserts both Info and Logs tabs visible explicitly. Combined coverage exercises all 5 tabs. Tab order is implied by the role-based getters but not explicitly asserted.

assertions.title: Clicking tab switches content without closing panel
test_names: Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
Step 7-8: Diff tab renders files, expand shows diff viewer
Step 9: Files tab renders file explorer
assertions.notes: Steps 6/7/8/9 each click a tab and assert the corresponding tabpanel is visible while continuing to interact with the open panel. Panel data-state=open is asserted between switches.

assertions.title: Switching agent resets activeTab to Info
assertions.notes: No spec opens agent A on a non-Info tab, then opens agent B and verifies activeTab resets to Info. agent-review-journey only exercises a single agent.

assertions.title: Close button dismisses panel
test_names: Step 10: Close panel
assertions.notes: Step 10 clicks getByRole('button', { name: 'Close panel' }) and asserts panel data-state=closed.

assertions.title: Pressing Escape closes panel
test_names: Step 10: Close panel
assertions.notes: Step 10 reopens the panel after the close-button check, then presses Escape and asserts data-state=closed.

assertions.title: Panel background click closes panel
assertions.notes: No spec clicks the overlay/background area to dismiss the panel. Step 10 uses only the close button and Escape.

assertions.title: Info tab displays Current Task section
test_names: Step 1-3: Open agent panel and verify Info tab
assertions.notes: Test asserts task title 'Fix authentication bug' is visible. Does not verify the labelled 'Current Task' section heading, the priority badge, or the clickable task link styling. Step 4-5 indirectly proves the title is a button by clicking it, but the section structure is not asserted.

assertions.title: Commit Status section shows sync status
test_names: Step 1-3: Open agent panel and verify Info tab
Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
assertions.notes: Both Step 1-3 and Step 6 assert '+3 ahead' and '-1 behind' badges visible in panel/gitPanel.

assertions.title: Commit list displays recent commits
test_names: Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
assertions.notes: Step 6 asserts three commit messages ('Add auth middleware', 'Fix token validation', 'Add auth tests') visible in gitPanel after clicking Git tab.

assertions.title: Show all commits button loads expanded commit list
assertions.notes: No spec exercises the 'Show all N commits' toggle or asserts the commit list expands/collapses.

assertions.title: Changes section lists modified files
test_names: Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
assertions.notes: Step 6 asserts 'Working Tree' label, 'src/auth.go', and 'src/auth_test.go' visible in gitPanel.

assertions.title: Agent Info metadata grid
assertions.notes: No spec asserts the dt/dd metadata grid (Path, Branch, Repos, Status, Task ID, Duration). Step 1-3 only checks task title and commit badges.

assertions.title: Open in Editor link
assertions.notes: No spec verifies the editor integration link or its href. Grep across e2e/ for 'Open in Editor' / 'open-in-editor' returns no matches.

assertions.title: Logs tab fetches agent terminal logs
test_names: logs tab exists and opens from agent detail panel
archive mode renders with refresh control
tmux mode renders live badge and token fetch path
talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
ember archive mode is stable when live tmux session is absent
assertions.notes: log-streaming asserts log-viewer testid visible after clicking Logs tab and exercises both archive and tmux modes including 'Archive snapshot' and 'Live (tmux)' badge labels. terminal-parity covers tmux mode end-to-end. Go coverage in handlers/misc/logs_test.go and log/streamer_test.go also validates server-side log streaming.

assertions.title: LogViewer displays log chunks with scroll follow
test_names: logs tab exists and opens from agent detail panel
archive mode renders with refresh control
assertions.notes: Tests verify log-viewer testid visible and data-state=connected. Scroll-to-top loading older logs (isLoadingMore spinner) and the auto-scroll/follow-tail behavior on new chunks are not asserted.

assertions.title: Refresh button visible in archive mode
test_names: archive mode renders with refresh control
archive refresh triggers another archive fetch
ember archive mode is stable when live tmux session is absent
assertions.notes: log-streaming asserts getByRole('button', { name: 'Refresh' }) visible in archive mode and verifies clicking it triggers a second /api/agents/ember/logs request (archiveRequests >= 2).

assertions.title: Git tab renders GitTab component
test_names: Step 6: Git tab renders commits and status
assertions.notes: Step 6 clicks Git tab, asserts #agent-panel-tabpanel-git visible and aria-selected=true, then asserts branch/commits/working-tree content.

assertions.title: Diff tab renders DiffTab component
test_names: Step 7-8: Diff tab renders files, expand shows diff viewer
assertions.notes: Step 7-8 clicks Diff tab, asserts #agent-panel-tabpanel-diff visible and aria-selected=true, verifies '3 files changed' summary, file rows, and that expanding a row reveals diff content with data-type='add' lines.

assertions.title: Files tab opens FileEditorPanel
test_names: Step 9: Files tab renders file explorer
assertions.notes: Step 9 clicks Files tab, asserts file-editor-panel testid visible, expands 'src' directory, clicks auth.go and verifies content loads.

assertions.title: EmbeddedTerminal renders header and terminal instance
test_names: talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
logs tab exists and opens from agent detail panel
renders tab bar with initial tabs
assertions.notes: EmbeddedTerminal is rendered in many specs (terminal-parity asserts terminal-container testid; log-streaming asserts log-viewer; tab-management asserts tab bar). However, no spec explicitly asserts the terminal-header testid as a structural element with all expected children together (backend label + connection dot + breadcrumb).

assertions.title: Terminal header shows backend name
assertions.notes: No spec asserts the BACKEND_DISPLAY label ('Claude'/'Codex'/'OpenCode') text inside terminal-header. Tab-management asserts tab labels, but the header inside EmbeddedTerminal showing the backend name is not exercised. visual-regression-terminal covers WelcomeBanner backend variants, not the EmbeddedTerminal header.

assertions.title: Terminal header shows connection state indicator
test_names: talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: terminal-parity asserts terminal-status-dot testid has data-status='connected' after WS opens. (terminal-tab-management asserts a tab-level status dot, which is a separate testid.)

assertions.title: Terminal header shows worktree path breadcrumb
assertions.notes: No spec asserts worktree-breadcrumb testid or the truncated path text. Grep for 'worktree-breadcrumb' in tests/e2e/ returns no matches.

assertions.title: EmbeddedTerminal reports connection state changes
assertions.notes: Callback contract is observable in Go via terminal/manager_test.go and handlers/terminal/terminal_test.go (broadcast/state). No Playwright spec verifies the onConnectionStateChange prop firing at the React layer.

assertions.title: TerminalInstance initializes xterm.js terminal
test_names: shows connecting overlay on first connection
hides overlay when connection succeeds
talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: Overlay-state assertions implicitly require xterm.js mounted in the DOM (terminal-container testid). terminal-parity captures a screenshot of the rendered xterm canvas.

assertions.title: Terminal applies FitAddon for auto-resize
test_names: split container renders with CSS grid columns
dragging divider right increases left pane ratio
split auto-disables when viewport width drops below 900px
assertions.notes: Split view tests verify CSS grid resize and divider drag, which require FitAddon to keep xterm in sync, but no spec explicitly asserts xterm cols/rows recompute after a resize event.

assertions.title: SearchAddon enables find-in-page
test_names: Ctrl+F opens search bar
Ctrl+F toggles search bar closed when open
Escape closes search bar when open
Enter in search bar retains focus
Shift+Enter in search bar retains focus
assertions.notes: Five tests in the 'Search shortcuts' describe block exercise the SearchBar / SearchAddon UI surface.

assertions.title: Terminal establishes WebSocket connection
test_names: hides overlay when connection succeeds
transitions through connecting → connected (overlay disappears)
talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: Disconnect-reconnect spec asserts connecting → connected transition (WS open). terminal-parity asserts terminal-status-dot data-status='connected'.

assertions.title: Terminal cursor blinks
assertions.notes: No spec asserts the cursorBlink xterm option or measures the cursor element animation.

assertions.title: Terminal connection state transitions: disconnected → connecting → connected
test_names: shows connecting overlay on first connection
hides overlay when connection succeeds
transitions through connecting → connected (overlay disappears)
assertions.notes: 'Connection State Transitions' describe block explicitly asserts the connecting overlay appears then disappears as state advances.

assertions.title: Connection state 'error' when WebSocket fails
test_names: shows error state after max initial attempts (3)
shows session expired after mid-session reconnect exhaustion
manual reconnect from error state
assertions.notes: Backoff Exhaustion describe block exercises the error state after max attempts and the manual recovery path from error.

assertions.title: Auto-reconnect on WebSocket disconnect
test_names: auto-reconnect fires after disconnect
assertions.notes: Network Disconnect describe block asserts auto-reconnect fires after a forced WS close.

assertions.title: Reconnect overlay shows attempt count
test_names: shows disconnected overlay when WebSocket closes
auto-reconnect fires after disconnect
assertions.notes: Disconnect overlay tests assert the overlay appears with retry/attempt messaging during reconnection sequences.

assertions.title: Reconnect button in overlay manually retries
test_names: reconnect button triggers new connection attempt
manual reconnect from error state
assertions.notes: Both tests click the reconnect button and assert a new connection attempt fires.

assertions.title: Terminal focus management
assertions.notes: No spec asserts terminal.focus() on click or keyboard activation. keyboard-focus-management.spec.ts covers modal focus traps and skip link only, not terminal focus.

assertions.title: Terminal blur removes caret
assertions.notes: No spec asserts blur behavior on the xterm caret.

assertions.title: TerminalView manages multiple terminal tabs
test_names: renders tab bar with initial tabs
marks active tab with aria-selected=true
Ctrl+1 switches to first tab
Ctrl+2 switches to second tab
Ctrl+3 switches to third tab
assertions.notes: tab-management asserts the terminal-tab-bar testid and renders three default tabs with labels. keyboard-shortcuts exercises switching between three tabs via Ctrl+N.

assertions.title: New tab button spawns new terminal session
test_names: clicking + button opens backend picker and creates a tab
assertions.notes: Test clicks terminal-new-tab-button, fills session-name-input, clicks Create, and polls for the role='tab' count to increase.

assertions.title: Tab bar shows backend brand color
test_names: shows connection state dots with data-status attribute
assertions.notes: tab-management asserts terminal-tab-status-* testid is visible with a data-status attribute, but does not assert the brand-dot computed background color matches BACKEND_DISPLAY (Claude=#D97706, Codex=#10B981, etc.). brand-dot testid exists in TerminalHeader.tsx but no spec inspects its color.

assertions.title: Tab close button removes tab
test_names: clicking close button removes the tab
close button hidden when only 1 tab remains
clicking Close removes the tab
assertions.notes: Tab Closing describe block clicks terminal-tab-close-* and asserts deleteCalls contains the session id; also verifies close button hidden for single-tab case.

assertions.title: Active tab switches automatically when current tab is closed
test_names: clicking close button removes the tab
split auto-disables when closing a tab reduces count below 2
assertions.notes: Tab close test verifies the closed tab disappears from deleteCalls but does not explicitly assert another tab becomes aria-selected=true. split-view test verifies side effects of tab-count change but not the active-tab promotion algorithm.

assertions.title: Close all tabs button closes all sessions
test_names: context menu shows expected options
assertions.notes: Test asserts context-menu-close-all option is visible in the right-click menu but does not click it or assert that all sessions are deleted.

assertions.title: Split view toggle enables two-pane mode
test_names: split toggle button is visible when 2+ tabs exist
split toggle button is disabled when only 1 tab exists
clicking toggle enables split view
clicking toggle again disables split view
assertions.notes: Four tests in 'Split view toggle' describe block fully exercise toggle visibility, enable, and disable.

assertions.title: Split pane divider is draggable
test_names: split-divider has role=separator and aria-orientation=vertical
dragging divider right increases left pane ratio
dragging divider left decreases left pane ratio
double-clicking divider resets to 50/50
assertions.notes: 'Divider resize' describe block covers drag right/left, double-click reset, and ARIA semantics.

assertions.title: Right pane tab selector switches which tab is shown on right
test_names: right pane shows non-active tab via split-pane-selector
selector lists all tabs except the active left tab
changing selector switches right pane tab
when active left tab changes, selector updates to exclude it
assertions.notes: 'Split pane selector' describe block fully covers selector population and pane-switching behavior.

assertions.title: Terminal session scrollback is persistent in split view
assertions.notes: No spec asserts xterm scroll position is preserved when a tab moves between left/right pane or when split is toggled. Session-storage tests cover layout persistence (split-view, ratio, right-tab) but not terminal scrollback.

assertions.title: Terminal tabs are loaded from server metadata on first render
test_names: renders tab bar with initial tabs
assertions.notes: setupTerminalMocks installs /api/terminal/state GET with active_tab plus per-session GETs. 'renders tab bar with initial tabs' iterates DEFAULT_TABS and asserts each terminal-tab-label-* renders with the server-provided label.

assertions.title: Active tab is restored from sessionStorage
assertions.notes: tab-management seeds active_tab via the /api/terminal/state mock (server source), not sessionStorage. split-view sessionStorage tests cover terminal-split-view / terminal-split-ratio / terminal-split-right-tab keys, not the active-tab restoration key.

assertions.title: Active tab is persisted to server on change
assertions.notes: trackers.statePatchCalls captures PATCH /api/terminal/state bodies in the mock harness, but no test asserts a specific PATCH body or count after a tab switch. The persistence path is exercised but not verified.

assertions.title: Dark theme vs. light theme color palette
assertions.notes: visual-regression-terminal screenshots SessionNamePrompt, WelcomeBanner, HelpPopover, and SearchBar in single-theme modes. No test compares xterm color palette across dark/light themes.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead button is visible in app header/layout
test_names: FAB button is visible with correct text
FAB has coral background color
Talk to Lead FAB has fixed positioning
assertions.notes: kanban-ui-redesign asserts talk-to-lead-button testid visible with text /Talk to Lead/ and coral rgb(240,93,70) background. kanban-redesign asserts position:fixed.

assertions.title: Button shows session count badge
assertions.notes: No spec asserts a session-count badge element on the Talk-to-Lead button.

assertions.title: Button aria-label includes session count
test_names: FAB has aria-label for accessibility
assertions.notes: Test asserts aria-label='Talk to Lead' (literal). Contract requires the aria-label to *include* a session count (e.g., 'Talk to Lead (3 sessions)'). The asserted value omits the count, so coverage is partial against the contract.

assertions.title: Clicking button opens Talk-to-Lead terminal panel
test_names: talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: Test clicks talk-to-lead-button and asserts terminal-panel-overlay testid becomes visible. Requires RUN_INTEGRATION_TESTS=1 (and tmux), but the test exists and exercises the click-open behavior end-to-end.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal is an EmbeddedTerminal instance
test_names: talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: Test renders terminal-container inside the talk overlay and verifies pixel-parity with the agent log terminal. Component identity (EmbeddedTerminal props/structure) is not asserted directly; parity with the agent terminal serves as indirect evidence.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal WebSocket URL is for lead session
assertions.notes: No spec inspects the WS URL constructed for the Talk-to-Lead terminal. Go coverage exists in handlers/terminal/lead_session_test.go and server/realtime/terminal_auth_test.go for the server-side endpoint, but the client URL contract is not E2E-asserted.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal accepts user input
assertions.notes: No spec types into the Talk-to-Lead terminal and asserts characters are echoed or sent to the backend.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead terminal auto-reconnects on disconnect
test_names: auto-reconnect fires after disconnect
reconnect button triggers new connection attempt
assertions.notes: terminal-disconnect-reconnect exercises auto-reconnect for a generic terminal context, not the Talk-to-Lead overlay specifically. The shared TerminalInstance code path is the same, but no spec asserts reconnect behavior with the talk-to-lead-button entrypoint.

assertions.title: Button is disabled if no backends configured
assertions.notes: No spec mocks a zero-backends configuration and asserts the talk-to-lead-button is disabled.

assertions.title: Talk-to-Lead panel can be closed
test_names: talk-to-lead and ember logs render the same terminal content
assertions.notes: Test clicks terminal-close-button and asserts terminal-panel-overlay aria-hidden='true'.
